After weeks of ChatGPT users being limited only by weekly caps, OpenAI announced today that it is reinstating the five-hour usage limits for Plus subscribers on Codex and ChatGPT Work. Here are the details.

The five-hour limit reinstatement applies to ChatGPT Plus subscribers

Thibault "Tibo" Sottiaux, OpenAI's head of Codex and ChatGPT engineering, announced tonight that starting tomorrow (the 25th), the five-hour usage limits on Codex and ChatGPT Work will be reinstated for Plus subscribers.

When users hit the five-hour or weekly cap, they can wait for the next cycle for usage to reset, or purchase additional credits. OpenAI also occasionally resets usage caps for free, and accumulated reset chances can be earned through specific promotions and referral offers.

However, in the past few weeks, OpenAI had temporarily removed the five-hour caps on Codex and ChatGPT Work, keeping only the weekly limits.

During this period, the company also reset users' weekly allowances ahead of schedule on multiple occasions to celebrate milestones, including reaching an additional one million active users across the two (now merged) platforms.

However, Tibo explained tonight on X:

"We will reinstate the five-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus accounts tomorrow. I mentioned this earlier, then postponed it. It is necessary for two reasons: (a) the five-hour cap helps us balance compute load, allowing us to maintain the generous level of our plans at the weekly level; (b) most Plus users are casual and newer users, who tend to accidentally burn through their entire weekly allowance and then feel confused, leading to a poor experience."

Tibo did not mention any changes to Enterprise or Edu accounts, which currently operate on a separate credits-based usage system.

Will the reinstatement of the five-hour limit on ChatGPT Work and Codex affect you? Let us know in the comments.
